description: A battalion executive officer must approve the loading assignments and sequence for three routine sustainment loads moving from a forward base to a support site, while recording the equipment and receiving controls needed for the movement.

shared_context.S1: Three loads are ready for movement to the support site: a clinic cold-chain pallet, a generator replacement pallet, and a routine administrative-supplies pallet.
shared_context.S2: The available transport vehicles are Truck T-1, Truck T-2, and Truck T-3, and each load must be assigned to one vehicle.
shared_context.S3: The support site will receive all three loads during the 0700-1300 movement period.
shared_context.S4: Maj. Patel approves the final vehicle assignments and loading sequence.
shared_context.S5: The battalion uses a pre-load coordination huddle before each sustainment movement, and Maj. Patel asks transportation, maintenance control, and medical logistics to report any current handling or receiving requirements before approval.

PF1.text: SFC Moreno confirmed during this morning's vehicle check that only Truck T-2 has a functioning refrigerated-power inverter approved for the clinic cold-chain pallet; the equipment note has not yet been added to the movement worksheet.

PF2.text: Sgt. Ellis confirmed from the current axle inspection that Truck T-3 is limited to 2,500 kilograms, while the generator pallet weighs 3,200 kilograms; the revised limitation is still awaiting entry in the vehicle status board.

PF3.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed with the receiving clinic that its fixed appointments are 0900 for the cold-chain pallet, 1030 for the generator pallet, and 1200 for the administrative-supplies pallet; the appointment sheet has not yet been cross-referenced with the movement plan.

acceptance_conditions: The clinic cold-chain pallet must be assigned to Truck T-2.
The generator replacement pallet must be assigned to Truck T-1.
The administrative-supplies pallet must be assigned to Truck T-3.
The loading order must be clinic, generator, then administrative supplies.
The plan must include a refrigerated-power verification, an axle-load verification, and a receiving-appointment confirmation.
At least one private operational fact must be spoken by its owner and cited by the decision-maker.

content_checks.C4: decisions['loading_order'] == ['clinic_cold_chain_pallet', 'generator_replacement_pallet', 'administrative_supplies_pallet'] or decisions['loading_order'] == ['clinic cold-chain pallet', 'generator replacement pallet', 'administrative-supplies pallet'] or decisions['loading_order'] == ['clinic cold-chain pallet', 'generator replacement pallet', 'routine administrative-supplies pallet']
content_checks.C5: any('refrigerated' in c['detail'] and 'inverter' in c['detail'] and 'T-2' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(('2,500 kg' in c['detail'] or 'weight' in c['detail'] or 'axle' in c['detail']) and 'T-3' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('0900' in c['detail'] and '1030' in c['detail'] and '1200' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed inverter status changes the clinic pallet assignment to exactly Truck T-2 and requires a commitment whose detail records the refrigerated inverter requirement for T-2.

The exact 2,500-kilogram limit on Truck T-3 versus the generator pallet's exact 3,200-kilogram weight changes the generator assignment to Truck T-1, leaves the administrative pallet on Truck T-3, and requires a commitment whose detail records T-3's weight limitation.

The exact receiving appointments of 0900, 1030, and 1200 change the loading order to clinic, generator, then administrative supplies and require a commitment whose detail records all three appointment times.
